examples.en: I stay close to good friends.
If you keep books close, your thinking gets deeper.
The closer children stay to nature, the healthier they get.
Don't go near the fire.

examples.ko: 저는 그 사람을 가까이하고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to be close to that person.
I've gotten into the habit of keeping exercise a regular part of my life.

explain: '가까이하다'는 사람, 책, 운동처럼 가까이 두고 자주 만난다는 뜻이에요. '책을 가까이하세요'는 책 읽는 습관을 들이라는 권유의 말이에요. 반대로 멀리하는 것은 '멀리하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: 가까이하다 means keeping something close and meeting it often, whether a person, books or exercise. '책을 가까이하세요' is advice to build a reading habit. The opposite, keeping away from something, is 멀리하다.

examples.ko: 저는 언젠가 우리나라를 대표할 선수가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: Someday I want to become an athlete who represents my country.
I'll say hello on behalf of our class.

examples.ko: 김치는 한국 음식을 가장 잘 대표해요.
examples.en: Kimchi represents Korean food better than anything.
Who represented our team at the meeting?

examples.ko: 이 그림은 한국 문화를 대표하는 작품이에요.
examples.en: This painting is a work that represents Korean culture.

examples.ko: 어떤 사람이 우리 모두를 대표하면 좋을까요?
examples.en: What kind of person would be good to represent all of us?

explain: 사람이 주어이면 여럿을 대신해서 앞에 나선다는 느낌이고, 음식이나 물건이 주어이면 그 나라나 문화를 떠올리게 한다는 느낌이에요. 같은 뿌리의 '대표적이다'는 '가장 좋은 예'라는 뜻으로 '대표적인 작품'처럼 써요. 회사에서는 사장님을 '대표님'이라고 부르기도 해요.
explain_en: With a person as the subject it means stepping forward on behalf of many; with food or objects it means they bring a country or culture to mind. The related '대표적이다' means 'a typical, leading example', as in '대표적인 작품'. In companies the boss is often called '대표님'.

examples.en: The fresh cream cake is soft and delicious.
Please put whipped cream on top of the coffee.
Please keep the fresh cream in the refrigerator.
The cream was too sweet, so I only ate a little.
Even just the cream by itself is rich and tasty.

examples.ko: 생크림과 우유는 비슷해 보여도 쓰임이 달라요.
examples.en: Fresh cream and milk look similar, but they are used differently.

explain: 우유에서 얻은 크림으로, 케이크나 빵집 메뉴에서 '생크림 케이크'처럼 자주 보여요. 거품을 낸 크림을 '휘핑크림'이라고도 해요. 영어 whipped cream과 완전히 같지는 않아서, 거품 내기 전의 크림도 생크림이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is cream made from milk and often appears on bakery menus as '생크림 케이크'. Cream that has been whipped is also called '휘핑크림'. It is not exactly the same as English 'whipped cream', because the cream before whipping is also called 생크림.

examples.ko: 이번 여행이 두고두고 이야깃거리가 될 것 같아요.
examples.en: This trip will probably be something to talk about for a long time.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 자리라서 이야깃거리를 찾기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's our first meeting, so it's hard to find things to talk about.
Celebrity news is always a good topic.
What else can we talk about besides the weather?

examples.ko: 그 영화가 요즘 친구들 사이에서 이야깃거리로 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: That movie has become a topic among friends lately.

examples.ko: 모임에서 나눌 이야깃거리 좀 생각해 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you thought of some topics to talk about at the gathering?

explain: '볼거리', '먹을거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙어서 이야기할 만한 재료라는 느낌이에요. 줄여서 '얘깃거리'라고도 해요. 비슷한 말로 '화젯거리'가 있어요.
explain_en: Like '볼거리' and '먹을거리', the '-거리' ending gives the feel of material worth talking about. It is shortened to '얘깃거리' in speech. A similar word is '화젯거리'.

examples.en: I leave a name out of this list.
It is ten thousand won excluding tax.
I excluded spicy food.
There is no reason to exclude him.
We open every day except Sunday.
Calculate after leaving out a few people.

explain: '빼다'는 일상에서 쓰고 '제외하다'는 공식적인 글과 설명에서 써요. '~을/를 제외하고'는 '~만 빼고'라는 뜻으로 아주 자주 나와요. 반대는 '포함하다'예요.
explain_en: The everyday verb for taking out is casual; this one is for formal writing and explanations. The pattern 'excluding X' is very common. Its opposite is the verb for including.

examples.en: I had lunch with my parents at a hanjeongsik restaurant.
In a hanjeongsik meal, a great many side dishes come out.
When guests come, we treat them to hanjeongsik.
Please make a reservation for the hanjeongsik course.
We chose a quiet hanjeongsik restaurant for the families' first meeting.
I wanted to eat hanjeongsik, so I went to Insa-dong.

explain: 밥, 국, 찌개와 여러 반찬을 한 상에 차려 주는 한국 전통식 코스예요. 간단한 '백반'보다 격식 있고 가격도 높은 편이라, 부모님 모시기나 상견례처럼 특별한 자리에서 자주 가요.
explain_en: It is a traditional Korean course with rice, soup, stew and many side dishes set out on one table. It is more formal and usually pricier than a simple '백반', so people often go for special occasions like taking parents out or a family-introduction meeting.
